mechanism_of_action.value: 12.1 Mechanism of Action Tralokinumab-ldrm is a human IgG4 monoclonal antibody that specifically binds to human interleukin-13 (IL-13) and inhibits its interaction with the IL-13 receptor α1 and α2 subunits (IL-13Rα1 and IL-13Rα2). IL-13 is a naturally occurring cytokine of the Type 2 immune response. Tralokinumab-ldrm inhibits the bioactivity of IL-13 by blocking IL-13 interaction with IL-13Rα1/IL-4Rα receptor complex. Tralokinumab-ldrm inhibits IL-13-induced responses including the release of proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines and IgE.

rescue_therapy_rules.value: If medically necessary (i.e., to control intolerable AD symptoms), rescue treatment for AD may be provided to trial subjects at the discretion of the investigator. Subjects who receive rescue treatment during the initial treatment period will be considered non-responders, but continue IMP if rescue consisted of topical medications. Investigators should limit the first step of rescue to topical medications, escalating to systemic medications only after at least 14 days without adequate response. Systemic corticosteroid/immunosuppressive rescue requires immediate IMP discontinuation; IMP may resume no sooner than 5 half-lives after the last dose of systemic rescue medication.
